message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.58,"fairness_assessment":"A multi-criteria social-choice process fairly compares visibility, recruitment, educational value, equipment urgency, and budget risk; it should avoid allowing the debate winner alone to determine the outcome.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Supports a full inter-city tournament with buffet and prizes to increase club visibility and recruit members.","influence":0.32},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Supports investing the entire budget in pedagogical equipment because current boards and related materials are worn.","influence":0.4},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Supports a hybrid allocation combining a smaller tournament with pedagogical equipment.","influence":0.28}],"recommended_resolution":"collaborative","governance_reasoning":"Use ranked or scored voting with explicit criteria and transparent cost estimates, followed by a joint review of feasibility. Agent B has the strongest debated case, but the unresolved trade-off between internal capacity and external growth favors a collaboratively designed allocation, potentially with safeguards such as a modest communication plan and a reassessment after implementation."}
